title: Kangra Fort
geometryBasis: The named twenty-control OSM archaeological precinct bounds the site. The separate sixty-control mapped masonry envelope and seventeen mapped pedestrian route controls govern the model. The outline is interpreted as rampart runs and ruined court walls.
sectionBasis: A steep-sided ridge carries the fort above the two rivers. Use the frozen relief at wall toes and the approximate northeastern approach datum. Gates and wall heights follow the selected modern photographs with bounded estimates.
limitations: The surviving western mapped masonry and northeast approach are represented. The outer mapped precinct line includes open slopes and access space.
Exact rampart height, parapet gaps, gate locations and temple foundations are estimates. Relative terrain is from an independent composite elevation field with coarse native cells.
Small reliefs and carvings are modeled in simplified original geometry. Former buildings destroyed in 1905, current vegetation and the separate ticket office and museum are outside scope.
